name: hazel_weir_central_procedural_graph
description: Optimized Central Procedural Graph featuring Peak Market Arbitrage, decoupled 10-hand workforce scaling, plot-capped land reinvestment, cluster harvesting transit optimization, and strict growth-cycle seed procurement horizons.

nodes.name: State & Balance Audit
nodes.description: Computes net available cash, shed fill percentage, wage liability, active shop contract demand, cyclical price premium ratios, and oracle price drop signals across market commodities.

nodes.name: Midnight Wage Reserve Defense
nodes.description: Protects payroll for all active hired hands. Enforces dynamic cash reserve locks and triggers pre-midnight surplus liquidation to prevent the 0-hand bankruptcy cascade.

nodes.name: Town Shop Demand Arbitrage
nodes.description: Preemptively matches unlocked town shop demand surges and fulfills mature high-margin crops (Carrots, Tomatoes, Pumpkins, Strawberries) through Day 30 to capture 2.0x-3.5x contract price premiums.

nodes.name: Shed Headroom Relief
nodes.description: Prevents silent 100/100 harvest discards at high shed capacity (>=90%) by clearing uncommitted inventory under strict price floors while protecting animal feed and active shop contracts.

nodes.name: Market Peak Arbitrage & Oracle Front-Run
nodes.description: Monetizes mature uncommitted shed surplus at cyclical price peaks (>=1.05x base price) with capped order slots, and reads 96-step TTM forecast to front-run opponent supply gluts.

nodes.name: Capital Reinvestment & Yield Scaling
nodes.description: Decouples workforce scaling into a low-hurdle sprint to 10 hands, scales contiguous plots up to 24 when current land is fully cultivated, and purchases commercial seeds strictly within maturation horizons.

nodes.name: Routine Farm & Workforce Execution
nodes.description: Executes field routines with cluster harvesting until worker capacity is full, batch shed drop-offs, watering, livestock feeding, seed planting, and ground maintenance.

attributes.guidance: Cancel non-essential purchases (BUY_SEED, BUY_ANIMAL, BUY_LAND, redundant HIRE); schedule worker harvest drop-offs before hour 21; enforce emergency liquidation of non-feed, non-contract inventory at hour >= 20 to guarantee payroll.
attributes.pitfalls: Never sell Wheat below dynamic livestock feed reserve (n_animals * 3, evaluating to 0 when holding zero livestock); do not rely on low-margin fertilizer sales to cover payroll deficits; never liquidate crops committed to active town shop delivery.

attributes.condition: has_unlocked_shops and (shop_deliverable_inventory > 0 or (net_available_cash >= 150.0 and day <= 27)) and day <= 30
attributes.guidance: Allocate up to 2-3 market slots to deliver matching mature shed inventory directly to town shops for 2.0x-3.5x premium through Day 30; procure shop-demanded seeds within growth cycle horizons (Pumpkins day <= 23, Tomatoes day <= 25, Carrots day <= 27) when surplus cash covers seed costs and wage buffers.
attributes.pitfalls: Do not commit seed capital if net cash falls below 1.25x midnight payroll reserve; never purchase shop seeds past their maturation cutoff day; never deliver unrequested or unreserved commodities to town shops; never hold shop produce past contract expiration windows.

attributes.guidance: Evict pending non-urgent buy orders to free order slots; execute batch sales of unreserved, non-shop surplus holdings with price >= 0.85 * base_price; only relax floor to 0.50 * base_price if shed_used >= 96 to strictly prevent 100/100 silent discard drops.
attributes.pitfalls: Never fire-sell at sub-0.85 base price unless shed fill is at acute overflow risk (>= 96%); never liquidate Wheat below dynamic livestock feed reserve (n_animals * 3); never evict produce allocated for active town shop fulfillment.

attributes.condition: (max_market_price_ratio >= 1.05 and uncommitted_surplus_count > 0) or (oracle_glut_risk >= 0.25 and current_price >= 0.75 * base_price)
attributes.guidance: Routinely clear mature uncommitted shed inventory at cyclical price premiums (current_price >= 1.05 * base_price) using 1-2 order slots to capture peak open market revenue; preemptively liquidate vulnerable commodities (Wool, Milk, Strawberry) if oracle detects opponent gluts before market prices collapse.
attributes.pitfalls: Do not commit more than 2 order slots per step to market sales to preserve worker execution bandwidth; never liquidate commodities committed to active town shop contracts; preserve livestock feed reserve (n_animals * 3); do not dump into collapsed sub-0.50 base price markets unless shed overflow is imminent.

attributes.condition: net_available_cash >= midnight_payroll_due * 1.20 + 75.0 and (hired_hands < 10 or (uncultivated_plots == 0 and total_plots < 24 and net_available_cash >= midnight_payroll_due * 1.30 + 180.0) or has_seed_deficit) and day <= 28
attributes.guidance: Decouple workforce scaling from land expansion: sprint workforce to the 10-hand cap with an accessible $75 reserve buffer over midnight wages. Invert land acquisition: purchase contiguous plots only when existing acreage is fully cultivated (uncultivated_plots == 0), total plots < 24, and surplus cash covers an expansion buffer (>= $180.0). Enforce strict seed maturation horizons: halt Pumpkin seed purchases at Day 23, Tomatoes at Day 25, and Carrots at Day 27; on Days 28-29 procure only fast Wheat seeds for empty plots. Restrict fertilizer purchasing until 10 hands and 16 plots are fully operational.
attributes.pitfalls: Never acquire land plots if uncultivated plots remain or if post-purchase cash drops below the $180 expansion buffer; do not acquire more than 24 plots to avoid worker transit decay; halt all land and seed purchases after Day 29 to maximize terminal cash accumulation.

attributes.guidance: Dispatch active hands strictly by operational priority: 1) Cluster Harvesting: Harvest mature crops on local plot clusters until personal carrying capacity is full or no adjacent ripe crops remain; 2) Batch Drop-off: Navigate to shed to deposit carried items ONLY when worker carrying capacity is full, during designated pre-midnight sweeps (hours 20-21), or in terminal steps (>= 712); 3) Water dry tilled and planted crops; 4) Feed hungry livestock; 5) Plant commercial seeds on moist tilled soil; 6) Weed clearing and ground tilling. Ensure all carried inventory is deposited at shed by step 716 for terminal liquidation.
attributes.pitfalls: Never route workers to shed with single harvested items when personal carrying capacity remains and adjacent harvestable crops exist; never prioritize weeding or tilling over harvesting or watering; ensure hands never idle while unharvested crops or dry plots remain; stagger worker paths to avoid shed entrance movement collisions.
